claims.statement: Rules 400 and 410 are internal underwriting controls: they govern whether an endorsement or deductible option may be selected and issued, but they do not grant coverage, change a policy deductible, or replace the applicable policy forms and endorsements.

Rule 400 requires review of every requested endorsement before binding or renewal, attachment only for an eligible risk supported by current and complete information, matching to the named insured, location, and insured property, and referral or suspension when eligibility or material facts are uncertain.

Rule 400 requires underwriting review of water and drainage, plumbing, roof, electrical, heating, use, occupancy, construction, prior losses, safeguards, and pending claims when those facts affect an endorsement, with referral for unresolved or adverse conditions.

Rule 400 prohibits using an endorsement to cure an ineligible risk, requires appropriate wording and no duplicate coverage, and requires effective-date alignment rather than retroactive attachment for a known loss circumstance.

Rule 400 requires approved processing, post-processing confirmation, renewal reassessment, and a clear record of the facts, rationale, and authority for every endorsement attachment, revision, or removal; unaddressed endorsement issues must be referred before issuance.

The authority matrix requires referral of a requested water-backup limit above $25,000 and prohibits binding the referred request until documented approval; this is an internal authority threshold, not a contractual water-backup limit.

Rule 410 sets the Section I all-other-perils deductible selection floor at $500, requires the selected option to be supported by risk characteristics, and requires the selection to be documented; this is an internal underwriting floor rather than a universal policy deductible.

Rule 410 requires use of an available deductible for the applicable coverage part, prohibits inferring an unstated deductible or combining terms from separate proposals, and requires referral of conflicting, unavailable, unsuitable, or exceptional deductible requests.

Rules 410.M and 410.N require application of the available named-storm minimum and wind-deductible ceiling but do not state numeric values; the applicable contract and state overlay supply the actual parameter, and requests outside normal authority require referral.

Rule 410 requires deductible selections to be consistent with submission, rating, issuance, location, occupancy, construction, protection, property use, and cause-of-loss information, and prohibits using a deductible to offset unacceptable property conditions or satisfy premium preference.

Rule 410 requires current-information review for deductible changes, prohibits retroactive application and post-loss revision based only on claim information, requires capture of the final selection before binding, and requires completion of deductible review before issuance.

HO 04 90 (2027-01) is effective only when attached, preserves unmodified policy terms, and contractually applies a $1,000 deductible to covered water-backup damage from the same occurrence; Rules 400 and 410 constrain attachment and internal selection without changing that contractual deductible.

HO 23 74 (2025-05) leaves the applicable policy deductible in force and applies it after the endorsement's roof-surfacing adjustment; Rules 400 and 410 constrain roof-related attachment and selection but do not replace the contractual deductible or settlement sequence.

HO 23 77 (2022-07) contractually applies a 2% to 10% windstorm-or-hail percentage deductible based on the applicable limit, while Rule 410.N constrains internal selection to the applicable underwriting ceiling and Rule 400 constrains weather-related attachment without changing the endorsement's stated percentage.

The endorsement-training workflow requires reading the complete endorsement rather than relying on its title, comparing its operative changes and deductible treatment with the request and existing endorsement set, and checking the complete package against the correct insured, policy term, location, property, effective date, schedules, and referenced pages. A listed-but-missing endorsement, an unlisted attachment, a blank or unclear schedule, or a mismatch between system text and issued wording must be clarified or reconciled before issuance.

For deductible-related attachments, the review must identify the loss cause and property to which the deductible applies, distinguish special deductible treatment from the general deductible, and confirm current risk facts, eligibility, selected wording, schedule details, and effective application before issuance; the issued wording must be preserved and corrected through the approved process rather than informal edits.

The HO-3 2024-03 base form makes the Section I deductible a contractual term with a minimum of $1,000, applies it to covered loss unless modified by endorsement, and requires application according to the policy terms and applicable endorsement; this contractual floor is distinct from Manual Rule 410.A's internal $500 selection floor.

When attached, HO 04 90 2027-01 provides its stated water-backup and sump-discharge-or-overflow coverage subject to a $10,000 section limit and supplies a $1,000 deductible applied to covered water-backup damage arising from the same occurrence; the endorsement's attachment language preserves unmodified policy terms and does not create a separate contract.

HO 23 74 (2025-05) changes settlement for covered roof surfacing without changing the applicable policy deductible; for composition shingle subject to its age-based treatment, the form uses a 20% payable percentage when Roof Age is at least twelve years, and the roof-surfacing adjustment is applied before the deductible.

HO 23 77 (2022-07) supplies an edition-specific contractual windstorm-or-hail percentage deductible range of 2% to 10%, calculated from the applicable limit and applied before payment; when a state amendatory form is also attached, its Declarations-based deductible terms must be checked separately rather than assuming the HO 23 77 range controls every policy. Texas HO 01 45, for example, requires its Declarations windstorm-and-hail deductible to be 1% to 10% and applies it separately from another deductible.
